deities: Narasimha (Vishnu avatar, as worshipper of Shiva)

history.dynasty: Somavamsi (Keshari) period; some sources suggest Bhaumakara
history.period: 8th-9th century AD (CONFLICT between sources: 8th c. vs 9th c. - verify)
history.summary: Ancient Panchayatana-style Shiva temple on a rocky island (foot-hill) in the middle of the Mahanadi river, accessible by boat from Gopinathpur village (6 km from Baramba) and now by road via the new Mahanadi T-Bridge. Famous for its unique Shaiva-Vaishnava sculptural fusion: Shiva is worshipped here by Narasimha, the man-lion avatar of Vishnu. The garbhagriha holds a Shivalinga on a yonipatta; it represents an early development of the pancharatha deula of Kalinga architecture. A protected monument of the Archaeological Survey of India; subsidiary shrines include Parvati (Annapurna), Vishnu, Ganesha, Surya, and Mahishamardini. Coordinates are from the ASI/IGNCA monument report and are approximate.

name: Singhanatha Temple
town_description: Baramba (also spelled Badamba) is a historic town and block in Cuttack district on the Mahanadi river. The Singhanath temple sits on an island in the river between Badamba on the left bank and Baideswar on the right bank. The area is a popular picnic and pilgrimage destination, best known for the T-shaped Mahanadi bridge that now connects the island to the mainland.
